title: Quinoa Stuffed Peppers
subtitle: Colorful, balanced, batch-friendly
description: Colorful, balanced, batch-friendly. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Prep pepper boats
steps.instruction: Halve bell peppers lengthwise; remove seeds. Blanch in boiling water 3 minutes; drain cut-side down on towels.

steps.title: Brown beef filling
steps.instruction: Brown ground beef with onion and garlic. Stir in cooked rice, crushed tomatoes, and Italian seasoning; simmer 10 minutes until thick.

steps.title: Fill and top
steps.instruction: Mound beef-rice filling into pepper halves on sheet pans. Top with shredded mozzarella.

steps.title: Bake until tender
steps.instruction: Bake at 375°F 25–30 minutes until peppers are tender and cheese bubbles. Stuffed Peppers slice cleanly if filling is tight — drain excess liquid before baking.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Quinoa Stuffed Peppers with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Portion bowls on the line with protein visible on top — crew eats with their eyes first.
Keep dressing and crunchy toppings in side bowls so greens stay crisp through second servings.
Line up Quinoa Stuffed Peppers on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Colorful, balanced, batch-friendly. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
